q: All are features of an innocent murmur EXCEPT:
o: It does not radiate to the back
It is soft without a thrill
e: Innocent murmurs are systolic (except a venous hum); diastolic murmurs are pathological.

q: Which is NOT a characteristic of a functional (innocent) murmur?
e: Innocent murmurs are short ejection (mid-systolic) murmurs.

q: Which murmur feature is NOT significant (can be innocent)?
e: A soft musical systolic murmur is Still's murmur.

q: Which statement about heart sounds in children is FALSE?
o: S2 is closure of the semilunar valves
S1 is closure of the AV valves
The first heart sound is normally widely split
A third heart sound may be normal
e: S2 splits physiologically; S3 can be normal; S4 is abnormal.

q: A PDA is closed medically by:
e: PGE keeps the duct open; prostaglandin inhibitors close it.

q: The most common congenital heart lesion in children is:
An oligaemic lung field on chest X-ray is typical of:
e: Right-to-left shunts with pulmonary stenosis reduce lung blood flow.

q: A plethoric lung field is seen in:
A newborn with Down syndrome should be screened for which heart lesion?
e: AVSD is strongly linked with Down syndrome.

q: A newborn whose mother has lupus has a heart rate of 55. The likely diagnosis is:
e: Anti-Ro/La antibodies damage the conduction system.

q: A newborn becomes cyanosed on day 3 as the duct closes. The first drug is:
e: PGE1 reopens the duct in duct-dependent lesions.
